rule: The project brief is complete and signed off before design starts: business goals, audiences, offer, positioning, primary conversion per page type, KPIs with baseline and target, budget, deadline and constraints.

Audiences are defined by their job to be done: problem, trigger, objections, decision criteria and search language. The basis is evidence (interviews, sales and support data, reviews, search data), not assumptions.

One positioning statement: for *[audience]* who *[need]*, *[brand]* is the *[category]* that *[key benefit]*, unlike *[alternative]*, because *[proof]*. It drives the home-page hero and the Organization description (GEO-05).
Analyze 3–5 business competitors and 3–5 search competitors (domains that rank for the core queries) on offer, positioning, content depth, UX, trust signals, technical health and link strength.

Keyword research per core topic: volume, difficulty, intent (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational), SERP features and whether an AI Overview appears. Group keywords into clusters and assign each cluster to exactly one URL in `url-map.csv`.
For each money query, record from the live results what ranks: format (guide, list, tool, category, product, local pack), depth and freshness. This sets the page type and the content brief.
Content gap analysis: topics search competitors rank for and we don't, prioritized by business value × feasibility.
The site type is chosen and its profile in [`site-types.md`](site-types.md) applied.
Prioritize pages by business value, demand and effort. Launch with the smallest set that covers the main conversion paths; no thin placeholder pages.
On existing sites, capture a baseline before work starts: traffic, conversions, rankings, Core Web Vitals, indexed pages and backlinks.
Record each target market's constraints: language, currency, legal requirements, payment and shipping norms.
Entity audit: how search engines and AI assistants describe the brand today (knowledge panel, AI answers), and the gap to the positioning statement.

SEO vendors get read-only Search Console access during audits, explain every change (especially with CMS or FTP access), and never guarantee rankings or sell "priority submit"; the site owner answers for their actions. Tool scores are heuristics: advice is checked against Google's documentation first.

Before any UI work, ask the client and record the answers in `DESIGN.md`: color palette (or offer 2–3 suggested palettes derived from brand, industry and audience, each contrast-checked), style direction (e.g. minimal/simple, modern translucent, bold/expressive, editorial, classic/corporate, playful), light, dark or both, density (airy or compact), 2–3 references the client likes and 1 they dislike (with why), what must stay untouched, 8–12 facts only this client has (name, place, materials, real numbers) and 2–3 personality words (not "clean", "modern", "premium"). Building starts only once answered or explicitly delegated.

`DESIGN.md` documents the brand for people and AI agents: intake answers (DES-13), positioning (STR-03), personality, voice and tone, logo use, color roles, typography, imagery, icons, motion and glossary.

Design tokens live in `tokens.json` (W3C DTCG format) in three tiers: primitive → semantic → component. Components use only semantic or component tokens, and code consumes them as CSS custom properties (TEC-04).
verify: Token build; grep CSS for raw hex values

rule: [house] Palette structure, 60-30-10: about 60 % primary family (the brand color and its tints set the identity: hero, brand bands, headers, illustrations; long-reading surfaces stay neutral for legibility), 30 % secondary (a supporting color for sections, cards and illustrations) and 10 % accent (reserved for the primary call to action and key highlights). A 9–10 step neutral scale for text, borders and backgrounds and semantic status colors sit outside the ratio. No second accent competing for attention.

Text color roles exist as semantic tokens: `text.default`, `text.secondary`, `text.muted`, `text.disabled`, `text.inverse`, `text.on-accent`, `text.link`, `text.link-visited` (if used) and `text.status.*`. Muted text never carries essential content. Each role is paired with its allowed backgrounds (DES-03).
Muted and secondary text use opaque tokens, never `opacity` or alpha on text, so contrast stays measurable (WCAG 1.4.3).
verify: Grep `opacity` on text selectors; contrast of computed colors

rule: [house] Tint ramps are built in a perceptual space (OKLCH, CSS Color 4) with chroma reduced near the lightness ends; the method is recorded in the token `$description`. Display type sets line height 0.95–1.1, letter-spacing ≥ −0.04 em, size ≤ 6 rem, ≥ 3× body on marketing pages, with no ascender/descender collision at 360 px.
verify: Token file; screenshots at 360 and 1440 px

rule: Every text/background pairing defined in tokens meets A11Y-07. Hover, focus, error, success and warning states have their own tokens. Dark mode, if offered, overrides the same semantic tokens.

Typography follows the golden-ratio scale: body 1 rem (16–18 px), H4 1.272 rem, H3 1.618 rem, H2 2.058 rem, H1 2.618 rem on desktop, one step smaller on mobile, fluid via `clamp()`. At most 2 families. Body line-height ≈ 1.6, headings 1.1–1.25, 45–75 characters per line (aim for ≈ 66; ≥ 35 on mobile, LAY-04).

Headings use weight 600–700, body 400, labels 500–600. Large headings get −0.01 to −0.02 em letter-spacing. Sentence case; no all-caps beyond short labels. `text-wrap: balance` for headings, `pretty` for body.

Every type role has a token with size, weight, line-height and letter-spacing: display, H1 (the page title), H2–H4 per DES-04, H5 1 rem/600, H6 0.786 rem/600, eyebrow/overline 0.786 rem/600 with +0.06–0.1 em tracking (stored as a rem dimension, DTCG) (all-caps allowed, ≤ 3 words), lead 1.272 rem/400 at line-height 1.5, body, small and caption 0.786 rem, label 0.786–1 rem/500–600, code (mono family), footer and legal text 0.786–0.875 rem. Nothing renders below 12.6 px (0.786 rem). Subheadings are real headings in the outline (A11Y-04); eyebrows and taglines are not.

Vertical rhythm: the space above a heading is at least φ times the space below it (H2 42/16 px, H3 26/10 px, H4–H6 26/6 px). Paragraphs are spaced 1 em, list items 6–10 px, figures and tables one φ step more than paragraphs. The first child of a container has no top margin. Use logical properties (`margin-block`).

Typographic details: tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) in tables, prices and counters; no justified text; `hyphens: auto` with the correct `lang` in narrow columns, never in headings; locale-correct quotes, apostrophes and dashes; non-breaking space between number and unit; headings wrap at ≤ 35 ch; link underlines with `text-underline-offset` 0.15–0.25 em; `font-synthesis: none` so the browser never fakes missing weights or italics.
Spacing uses only the φ scale. Space inside a group is at least one φ step smaller than space between groups (PSY-02).

Layout: 12-column grid on desktop (columns per tier: LAY-02) with content-driven breakpoints, container max 1200–1280 px, text column ≈ 66 ch, asymmetric splits at 61.8/38.2, section padding 68–110 px on desktop, 68 on tablet and 42 on mobile (LAY-05), shared alignment lines, whitespace instead of decoration.

Emphasis budget: at most three emphasis levels per section (primary, secondary, tertiary), adjacent heading levels differ by at least one type step, one focal point per view (PSY-03). Bold marks ≤ 10 % of running text, italics only for titles and terms, underline only for links (DES-19), all-caps only for labels (DES-24). The accent stays reserved for the primary action (DES-14).

Alignment: running text is start-aligned (left, or right in RTL, I18N-10). Centered text only for headings and blurbs of ≤ 3 lines. One alignment axis per section. Numbers in tables align to the end (CMP-04).

Shape: one radius family from the φ scale applied by role (controls 10, cards 16, large panels 26, tags pill); nested radius = outer radius − padding. One elevation system (≤ 3 shadow levels, or borders), not mixed at random. One icon set with one stroke width, sized 1–1.272 em of the adjacent text.

Buttons come in three tiers only: primary (filled accent), secondary (outline or tonal), tertiary (text). Min height = touch target (LAY-08), horizontal padding 16–26 px from the φ scale, verb label (UX-15) at 1 rem/600, all states (DES-06) and a visible focus ring. At most one primary per view (UX-06). Icon-only buttons have an accessible name.

Links in running text are underlined (or carry another non-color cue) and differ from body text in color. They have hover and focus-visible states, and say when they open a new tab. Link text names the target (A11Y-15). Links navigate; buttons act.

Inputs: label above the field, height `size.control.md` (touch target, LAY-08), one border style, focus ring in the focus token, error state with icon and text (A11Y-17). A placeholder never replaces the label.

Icons: one set on a 24 px grid (sizes 16, 20, 24, 32), colored with `currentColor`. Decorative icons are `aria-hidden`; standalone icons have an accessible name (A11Y-06). Only universally known icons (search, menu, close, home, cart) stand without a text label. Directional icons mirror in RTL (I18N-10).
SVG parts that scale or rotate set `transform-box: fill-box` and an explicit `transform-origin`; motion starts from its physical anchor (a menu from its trigger, a popover from its arrow).
verify: Chrome and Safari check; grep SVG transforms

rule: Icon sourcing: one library per site from [`reference/assets/`](../reference/assets/README.md), imported icon by icon as inline SVG (tree-shaken); no icon fonts, no full-set bundles, no mixing sets. Size and stroke come from `iconSize`/`iconStroke` (DES-33). The library and license are recorded in the third-party inventory (TEC-20) and the handover (TEC-27).
Component inventory: every component documents its states (default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error, empty) and its responsive behavior.
Each component is built once and reused, in the design library and in code. No one-off variants without review.

The token set is complete. Besides color, type, space and radius, it defines: breakpoints (LAY-01), content widths (LAY-03), z-index (base 0 · raised 10 · dropdown 100 · sticky 200 · overlay 300 · modal 400 · toast 500 · tooltip 600), border widths (1 and 2 px), focus ring (2–3 px width, 2 px offset, `color.focus`), shadow levels (≤ 3, DES-17), scrim opacity (0.5–0.7), motion durations and easings (DES-08), aspect ratios (1:1 · 4:5 · 4:3 · 3:2 · 16:9 · φ 1.618:1) and icon sizes (DES-33). Components use no raw values (DES-02).

Forced-colors mode (`@media (forced-colors: active)`) stays usable: buttons, cards and inputs keep visible borders (transparent borders, not only backgrounds), focus stays visible, icons use `currentColor`, and no information lives only in background images or shadows.
verify: Windows contrast theme or DevTools emulation

rule: Dark mode, if offered (DES-12): surfaces get lighter with elevation instead of relying on shadows, accent and status colors are adjusted to pass A11Y-07 on dark surfaces, no pure black (#000) behind long text, logos and images have dark-safe variants, and every component is checked in both themes.

Charts: a categorical palette of ≤ 8 colors that stays distinguishable with color-vision deficiencies, marks ≥ 3:1 against the background (A11Y-07), meaning never in color alone (direct labels, patterns or shapes), direct labels over legends, bar axes starting at zero, and a text summary or data table (A11Y-06). The chart type follows the data (trend: line; comparison: bar; part of a whole: bar, or a pie of ≤ 5 slices); the title states the finding and the subtitle the data, place and period; one highlight color, the rest neutral.

Handoff: design files use variables and styles named and structured exactly like `tokens.json`. Tokens flow from one source into CSS by a build step ([`tokens_to_css.py`](../scripts/tokens_to_css.py) → `tokens.css`); nobody copies values by hand.
verify: Compare design variables with the token file; `tokens_to_css.py --check`

rule: State tokens: every interactive token has hover, pressed, focus, disabled and (where it applies) selected values. A hover effect combines at most two of: one color step, a state layer (hover ≈ 8 %, pressed ≈ 12 % opacity), a lift ≤ 2 px, a scale ≤ 1.02, one shadow level up, an underline change. Timing comes from the transition tokens (DES-08); hover effects are gated by LAY-08 and never the only state cue.

Elevation: `shadow` tokens for three levels plus an inset, each tied to one use (level 1 card, level 2 dropdown and popover, level 3 dialog and toast) and matched to z-index tokens (DES-30). No other shadows. Dark mode raises surfaces by lightness instead (DES-32).
verify: Token file; CSS grep for raw `box-shadow`

rule: Borders and outlines: composite `border` tokens (color, width, style) for default, subtle, divider and input states (default, hover, focus, error, disabled). The focus outline is a token (2 px solid, 2 px offset, inset variant for clipped containers) that reaches 3:1 against every surface it appears on (A11Y-07).

Every type role (DES-24) is one composite `typography` token (family, size, weight, line height, letter spacing). Fluid roles record their mobile and desktop sizes for `clamp()` (LAY-04). Components reference the composite, not single properties.

Themes override semantic tokens only, never primitives or components: a dark set if dark mode is offered (DES-12, DES-32), an optional high-contrast set, and a documented forced-colors mapping to CSS system colors (DES-31). Every semantic color exists in every theme.
verify: Token build per theme; contrast check per theme

rule: Token governance: names follow `tier.category.role.state` in lowercase kebab case; semantic and component tokens carry a `$description`; retired tokens stay one release with `$deprecated` naming the replacement; changes are logged in `DESIGN.md`. A validator checks references, types, units and contrast pairs in CI.

No generic AI look: no unchanged default component-library styling, decorative purple-blue gradients or glows, emoji used as icons, everything centered, identical icon-card grids, stock 3D illustrations, mixed radii and shadows, random accent colors or filler copy; gradient text, colored glows, radial blobs, orbs and mesh washes; sparkle, wand or robot icons standing for "AI"; skeleton bars or fake terminals as product shots; the template stack (hero, logo bar, 3 icon cards, 3 steps, 3 prices, FAQ, 4-column footer) when the content has another shape; and the opposite failure, an identity-free grey default. Every visual choice traces back to `DESIGN.md` and real content.
verify: Design review against this list; swap test: put a competitor's logo and name in. If layout, palette, type and copy still fit, the direction was not applied

rule: Translucent style (if chosen): translucency only for navigation, overlays and floating surfaces, never behind long text. `backdrop-filter` gets an opaque `@supports` fallback, contrast is measured against the worst-case background (A11Y-07), blur ≤ 20 px.

[house] Ornament budget: decorative backgrounds (grid, dots, noise, mesh) only when `DESIGN.md` names the motif, and never three or more of glass, mesh, glow, noise and grid in one view. No accent stripe on card edges, no arrow on every button, no pulsing dot without a live state, no card inside a card, no pill above the H1 repeating it, no "New/Beta/AI" badge without a real status. Eyebrows add information the heading lacks; section numbers only where order matters, as a real `<ol>`.
verify: CSS grep (`background-clip: text`, `border-left` on cards, `infinite`); DOM probe for nested cards

rule: [house] Real imagery: hero and feature visuals show the real product (screenshot or live UI with real data), a real photo, or nothing; no grey skeleton bars, fake terminals or invented dashboards (CON-21). One image treatment per site (untouched or one shared grade). Feature icons depict what their label names. No look-alike of another named product unless the brief asks for it.

Browser-drawn surfaces follow the theme: `color-scheme` on `:root` per theme, `<meta name="theme-color">` with light and dark `media` variants, `::selection` from `color.selection` (text ≥ 4.5:1), `accent-color` and `caret-color` from the accent, `scrollbar-color` from neutrals, and explicit colors on native `<select>`/`<option>`.
verify: Screenshots of selection, checkbox, range, select, scrollbar and date input in both themes

rule: Motion has a purpose (feedback, state change, orientation): UI transitions 150–300 ms, large elements ≤ 500 ms; entering elements decelerate (`easing.enter`), leaving elements accelerate (`easing.exit`) and run no longer than their entrance, on-screen moves use `easing.standard`, `linear` only for progress and scroll-linked motion. Movement animates only `transform` and `opacity`; color, border and shadow change only as state changes at ≤ `duration.fast`; never `width`, `height`, `top`/`left`, `filter` or `transition: all`. A new interaction cancels a running animation. Reduced-motion variant per A11Y-26.
verify: Grep `transition: all` and raw `cubic-bezier`; Performance panel; OS setting

rule: Micro-animations make the interface feel alive without distracting: hover and press feedback on interactive elements, smooth state changes, reveal on scroll within the entry range or once via IntersectionObserver (≤ 400 ms, stagger ≤ 60 ms); the hidden start state exists only inside the animation or a script-added class, so content stays visible without JavaScript or support. Never animate the LCP element in, no scroll-jacking, no looping motion near text, nothing that delays content or input (PRF-01). Prefer CSS and the Web Animations API; reuse a small set of animated components.

Motion timing: duration follows the area moved (icon, switch, tooltip `fast`; card, popover, panel `base`; drawer, sheet, full-width `slow`/`large`, never > 500 ms), listed per component in `DESIGN.md`. Hover, press and focus feedback has no delay. A stagger group ends within 500 ms ([house]: ≤ 5 steps, DOM order, mirrored in RTL, exits don't stagger). One focal motion per view; at most one looping decoration, paused off-screen and in hidden tabs; no overshoot or bounce on errors, destructive actions or text.
verify: Computed durations vs. the table; `document.getAnimations()` while scrolling

rule: Animation stack: use the first option that does the job: CSS and the Web Animations API ([`motion.css`](../templates/motion.css)), then AutoAnimate or Motion, then GSAP or Lottie with a reason recorded in the brief. Durations and easings come from the transition tokens; every animation has a `prefers-reduced-motion` variant (A11Y-10); animation JavaScript counts against the JS budget (PRF-04).
verify: Code review; bundle analyzer; reduced-motion check

rule: Illustration and animated assets: one illustration style per site from own work or [`reference/assets/`](../reference/assets/README.md), recolored to the tokens. Lottie files load lazily below the fold with a static poster, stay ≤ 150 KB ([house]), and never carry essential information alone (A11Y-06).
Prefer authentic imagery (own team, products, customers) over stock. Art direction, aspect ratios and focal points are defined; image licenses are recorded (TEC-27).

[house] Brand assets: SVG logo; favicon set declared on the home page, one per hostname, at a stable URL that Googlebot-Image may crawl: a square ICO containing ≥ 48 px images plus a 192 px PNG (Google recommends larger than 48×48 and lists BMP, GIF, ICO, PNG, JPEG, PPM, TIFF, not SVG; an SVG icon is an optional extra); 180 px apple-touch icon; manifest icons 192 and 512 px; and a default plus per-page Open Graph image (≥ 1200 px wide, 16:9: 1200×675, SEO-19).
verify: [`head.html`](../templates/head.html) links resolve; URL Inspection on the home page

rule: Before launch, production CSS is checked against `DESIGN.md`: no colors, font sizes, spacings or radii outside the tokens.
Dark mode follows `prefers-color-scheme` and offers a user toggle.

The information architecture comes from `url-map.csv` and user tasks: a shallow hierarchy, one clear parent per page, and labels in the users' own words (validated by tree test, card sort or search data).
Primary navigation has ≤ 7 top-level items in the same position and order on every page and marks the current section. The footer repeats key links, contact and legal pages.

Pages at depth ≥ 2 (house heuristic) show breadcrumbs that follow a typical user path, marked up as `BreadcrumbList` (≥ 2 `ListItem`s with `name`, `position` and `item`; the last `item` may be omitted).
Sites with more than about 50 content pages offer site search. The results URLs are blocked in robots.txt (SEO-03).
Mobile first: designed and built for 360 px first. No horizontal overflow at the QA-02 widths. No function depends on hover.
Each page has one primary call to action. It is visually dominant and repeated after long content; secondary actions stay visually subordinate.
On key pages, the first screen says what it is, who it is for and the main benefit, and shows the primary call to action, with no scrolling needed.
Trust signals sit near decisions: reviews with their source, client logos with permission, certifications, guarantees, real contact details, prices or pricing logic.

Forms ask only for necessary fields, in a single column, with correct input types and `autocomplete`. Fields validate inline on blur. The submit label names the outcome ("Request quote"). After submitting, the user sees a confirmation with next steps.
Every view has defined empty, loading and error states. The 404 page offers search or key links (TEC-05).
No dark patterns: fake urgency or scarcity, confirmshaming, pre-checked add-ons, hidden costs, back-button hijacking (SEO-33) or consent nudging (PRV-02).
Contact options (phone, email, form, chat) are visible in a consistent place (A11Y-19), and expected response times are stated.
Before launch, at least 5 target users test the core tasks. Every issue that blocks completing a task is fixed.
Conversion paths (entry page → call to action → form → confirmation) are mapped and instrumented (MSR-08). Funnel drop-off is reviewed monthly.

Microcopy: buttons and links say what happens as verb plus object (standalone "Get started", "Learn more", "Submit" fail unless the visible text names the target, WCAG 2.4.4), error messages say how to fix the problem, and terms come from the glossary in `DESIGN.md`.

If A/B tests run: enough traffic and a written hypothesis, metric and sample size. Variants carry a canonical to the original (not `noindex`) and use temporary (302) redirects. Googlebot sees the same variants as users (no cloaking, no robots.txt-based serving), and finished tests are removed promptly.

No full-page overlay or dialog hides content on landing (app install, newsletter, promo): use small banners. Never redirect users to a separate page for consent or input; mandatory gates (age, consent) overlay the content instead. Ads and pop-ups never obstruct or distract from the main content.
verify: Manual check at 360 and 1440 px in a fresh session

rule: Forms and editors with unsaved, non-autosaved input warn before leaving. The `beforeunload` listener exists only while the form is dirty, so clean pages keep the back/forward cache (PRF-16).
verify: Edit a field and reload: native prompt; clean page: no prompt; bfcache test passes

rule: Destructive or irreversible actions name the object and the consequence in the message and the button (never Yes/No/OK). Reversible actions offer Undo instead of a dialog. Legal, financial and data-submission steps are reversible, checked or confirmed (WCAG 3.3.4).
verify: Delete, cancel and submit walkthrough per flow

rule: [house] View state that changes what the page shows (filters, sort, query, tab, page, a shareable open panel) lives in the URL: refresh, a copied link and back/forward restore the same view. View changes use `pushState`, transient refinements `replaceState`. URL forms follow SEO-12 to SEO-14.
verify: Paste the URL in a new tab: same view; back restores the previous filter

rule: Back and forward restore scroll position and expanded or filtered state, including client-routed pages and "load more" lists; `history.scrollRestoration` stays `auto` unless restore is implemented.
verify: Scroll a list, open an item, press back: same position

rule: Client-side route changes update `<title>` (WCAG 2.4.2) and the H1, move focus to the new H1 or announce the page in a live region, and reset scroll unless back/forward restores it.

*(dashboards)* A KPI change is colored by good or bad for that metric, not by up or down; zero and missing changes are neutral; the comparison window is stated ("vs. prior 30 days"); decimals are fixed per metric; chart scales stay visible; forecasts are dashed and labelled.

*(shop)* Product page: name, price including VAT with a shipping link, availability, variant selectors and add-to-cart are visible without scrolling on mobile and desktop. Below them: images with zoom, description, specifications (CMP-04), shipping and return summary, and reviews (PSY-12). Choosing a variant updates URL (SEO-49), price, image and availability; unavailable variants are marked, never silently hidden.
*(shop)* Shipping costs and delivery time appear on the product page or in the cart before checkout starts. No fee is added at the last step (UX-11, PSY-13, PRV-12).

*(shop)* Cart: every line shows image, variant, quantity (editable) and price, with a remove control. The cart shows subtotal, shipping, tax and total, survives a new session, and has one primary call to action (checkout). [house] A promo-code field is a collapsed link, not an open field.

*(shop)* Checkout: guest checkout (account offered after purchase), a single page or ([house]) ≤ 5 steps with progress (CMP-19), `autocomplete` and address lookup, billing address = shipping address by default, payment methods common in the target market including wallets, the order summary visible throughout, no re-entry of data already given (A11Y-18) and edits without data loss. The final button follows PRV-12.
verify: Test order on mobile and desktop

rule: *(shop)* Listings and filters: filters fit the category; on mobile they open in a drawer (CMP-12) with an apply button. Active filters show as removable chips (CMP-05) with the result count; sort options are offered. Listings show price, availability and rating ([house] 2 columns on mobile). A no-results state suggests removing filters. Facet URLs follow SEO-13.
*(shop)* After purchase, a confirmation page and email show order number, items, total, delivery estimate, next steps and contact (PSY-11).

On-site search (where offered) tolerates typos and synonyms, suggests after 2–3 characters ([house]), and turns zero results into help: suggestions, popular categories and contact. Site-search events are tracked (MSR-09); zero-result queries are reviewed monthly. Result pages follow SEO-63.
verify: Search test with typos; query report

rule: *(chat)* Chatbots and AI assistants: disclosed as AI before the first message (PRV-13), with a visible route to a human or contact form at any time (UX-12). Answers come from the site's current content and link to the source page; prices, terms and legal information never live only in the chat. The widget works by keyboard and screen reader, announces messages in a live region (A11Y-17), stays within LAY-20 without covering the primary action, and loads third-party code only after consent or interaction (PRF-13, PRV-01). The privacy policy covers chat logs: purpose, retention, and no model training on them without consent (PRV-04). Generating answers can be stopped, each answer offers "helpful / not helpful" and a correction route, and streamed text is announced once per message, not per token (WCAG 4.1.3). Answer accuracy is reviewed monthly from the logs.
verify: Keyboard and screen reader test; log review

rule: *(SaaS, web app)* Onboarding: sign-up asks only for what the first session needs (email plus password, passkey or SSO). A trial that needs a card says so on the pricing page. The first run leads to one defined activation event in ≤ 5 steps through empty states (CMP-21) and an optional, skippable checklist or tour; advanced features appear progressively. Activation is a key event (MSR-08) and its drop-off is reviewed (UX-14).
[house] Each indexable URL serves one primary intent and one query cluster (`url-map.csv`). No two URLs target the same intent.
Every page gets a content brief before writing: intent, audience, primary query, questions to answer, unique angle or evidence, outline, internal links, call to action, schema type.
[house] Each core topic has a pillar page that links to cluster pages, each answering one specific sub-question (SEO-23).
[house] People-first: every page adds something not available elsewhere, such as first-hand experience, original data, expert insight, worked examples or tools. No rewritten commodity content.

[house] Trust (E-E-A-T): the site shows who is behind it (About, team, Impressum). Each article has a byline linking to an author page with credentials. Sources are cited for facts, figures and claims. No fabricated authors: no made-up names, AI-generated headshots or false credentials.

Articles show their published and updated dates, and `datePublished`/`dateModified` markup equals them (timezone included, no future dates). "Updated" changes only after a substantive edit, never for a date bump alone.
Answer first: lead with the direct answer or key takeaway, then the detail. One idea per paragraph. Subheadings mirror real user questions. Use lists and tables for comparable data.

Use plain, active language at the audience's reading level and the voice defined in `DESIGN.md`. No filler introductions. Objective, not promotional: every claim carries a fact, and the hype words in the AI-writing checklist are absent (NN/g measured objective copy as more usable).

AI-assisted content gets expert review, a fact check of every claim and an original contribution. Disclose AI use where readers would expect it (and per PRV-13). Review also covers `<title>`, meta description, structured data and alt text. In Merchant Center feeds, AI-generated images carry IPTC `DigitalSourceType` `TrainedAlgorithmicMedia`; AI-written product titles and descriptions are labeled as such in Merchant Center. Never publish at scale without review (SEO-33).
Prefer original images and diagrams to stock. Use captions where they add context. Videos get a transcript and chapter markers. Alt text follows A11Y-06.
Health, finance, legal and safety topics (YMYL) are written or reviewed by named, qualified experts.
Each page has an owner and a review date. YMYL pages are reviewed every 6 months, all others at least yearly. Dated markup (events, offers, jobs) is kept current.

Every quarter, pages with falling traffic or rankings are reviewed for usefulness. Improve them first; merge (301) or remove (410) only content that cannot be salvaged. Never add or delete content in bulk to look "fresh", and a drop after a core update alone is no reason to delete. No thin or outdated page stays indexable.
An editorial calendar follows the clusters and business priorities. Every piece has a distribution plan (newsletter, social, outreach).

Reviews, comparisons and best-of pages show first-hand evidence: own testing or measurements, benefits and drawbacks, why an item is best, alternatives or several sellers. No thin summaries or copied merchant text.

[house] Every indexable URL returns `200`, is not blocked by robots.txt and has its content in the initial HTML response. Key information is real text in the DOM, not only in images, video, canvas or CSS `content`.

[house] `/robots.txt` controls crawling only with `user-agent`, `allow`, `disallow`, `sitemap` (Google ignores other lines; ⚗ GEO-16 lines are optional extras). It lists the sitemap as an absolute URL, stays under 500 KiB, and never blocks CSS, JS, images or APIs needed to render a page (blocking small, frequently requested non-rendering assets is allowed). It blocks state-changing URLs (cart, account, comment post) and internal search results. `*` does not match AdsBot; name it explicitly. Template: [`robots.txt`](../templates/robots.txt).

[house] Every host that serves pages (each subdomain, protocol and port) has its own `/robots.txt` at its root. It returns `200`; a 4xx (except `429`) counts as "no rules", while `429`, a `5xx` or a timeout halts crawling of the host for up to 12 h. It is never used to hide private content (use authentication).
Production carries no leftover `noindex`, `Disallow: /` or password protection from staging.
One canonical host: HTTPS plus either `www` or apex. Every other variant answers with a single 301 to it.

The certificate matches the host, with no insecure sub-resources (except images) and no HTTPS→HTTP redirects. Canonicals are never steered with robots.txt, `noindex` or the Removals tool.

rule: [house] The XML sitemap (UTF-8, absolute URLs, at the site root) lists only canonical, indexable `200` URLs. `lastmod` changes only on significant edits, never for copyright-year or template changes. No `priority` or `changefreq` (Google ignores them). Max 50,000 URLs or 50 MB per file; use a sitemap index above that.

Missing content returns `404`/`410`, or a 301 to a true equivalent. No soft 404s: no `200` that serves an error page or the home page. Empty search, filter and category results return `404` or `noindex`. Client-routed apps send error routes to a URL the server answers with `404`, or add `noindex` via JS.

Permanent moves use server-side 301/308: one hop, no loops (legacy chains at most 3 hops). Genuinely temporary redirects (outage notice, A/B test) use 302/307 so Google keeps the original URL. JavaScript or meta-refresh redirects only where server-side is impossible. Internal links point to final URLs.

[house] Primary content, links, canonical and robots meta are in the server-rendered or prerendered HTML. JavaScript may add a canonical only if it equals the HTML one (or the HTML has none; exactly one tag) and may add `noindex` to error pages. A `noindex` in the source HTML is never removed by JS (rendering may be skipped), so never ship it on pages meant to be indexed.

rule: Navigation uses crawlable `<a href>` links with real URLs. No `#!`, `javascript:` hrefs, `onclick`-only, `routerLink`-only or form-based navigation, and no `#` fragments for routing or content states (History API paths instead).

URLs are lowercase, hyphenated, descriptive (words, not opaque IDs) and use one trailing-slash form (lowercase and slash form are house style). Parameters are `?key=value&key2=value2` (multiple values comma-separated). Internal links carry no session or tracking parameters, are root-relative or absolute (never `../`) and percent-encode non-ASCII characters.

Facet, filter and sort URLs not meant to rank are disallowed in robots.txt (or use `#` fragments); canonical and `nofollow` only reduce crawling slowly. Facets meant to rank are crawlable, use `&` parameters or fixed-order path segments, and return `404` for empty combinations. Never use `noindex` to steer canonicals. No infinite crawl spaces (`nofollow` endless calendar pages).

rule: Paginated lists use linked pages (`?page=2`), each self-canonical, never all canonical to page 1. Multi-part articles never canonicalize to part 1. Infinite scroll and "load more" have crawlable paginated URLs behind them (absolute page numbers, History API updates).

Crawl waste: internal search results, cart and action URLs ("sign up", "buy now"), session IDs and other infinite URL spaces ([house] plus checkout and account areas) are blocked in robots.txt (never combined with `noindex`, SEO-02), kept out of sitemaps and, where possible, out of internal links.
The mobile version carries the same primary content, headings, title, meta description, structured data, image alt text, robots meta and crawlable links as desktop.

Title and visible `<h1>` agree, match the page's language and script, and are not half-empty (separator plus brand only). Paginated sequences may share titles.

Each indexable page has a unique meta description that summarizes the page (about 120–160 characters is a house heuristic; Google sets no limit). Generate from page data if needed; keyword lists are less likely to be shown. Home and aggregation pages get site-level text; paginated sequences may share one.
[house] One `<h1>` matching the page topic. Google ignores heading count and order; this is house style and accessibility (A11Y-04).
[house] The page's primary query (from `url-map.csv`) shows up naturally in the title, H1, slug and first paragraph. No keyword stuffing.

Templated titles and descriptions are generated from the page's real data: no boilerplate shared across a section, no long titles that differ by one word, and no claims the page can't back up (mention "video" only if the page has one).
