Claimed Googlebot traffic is verified by reverse+forward DNS or Google's published IP ranges, never by user agent alone.
verify: URL Inspection live test; GSC Crawl stats; WAF logs

rule: Crawlers are throttled only with `503` or `429` (plus `Retry-After`) and for at most 1–2 days. A `4xx` other than `429` never reduces crawl rate, and `crawl-delay` is ignored. For a crawl spike, check access logs for facets and calendars first.

Planned downtime or closure keeps pages online and indexable: disable the cart, add a banner with `data-nosnippet`, update availability and opening-hours markup. A full shutdown of 1–2 days returns a static `503` with `Retry-After` (robots.txt stays `200`); never `403`/`404`/`410`, `noindex` or `Disallow: /`. Longer closures keep an indexable `200` placeholder.

A host or CDN change without URL changes is tested on a temporary hostname with `noindex`, checked with URL Inspection, keeps Search Console verification, drops temporary blocks, and keeps the old host until its traffic is zero.
Responses send `ETag` (preferred by Google) or a valid HTTP-date `Last-Modified` and answer `If-None-Match`/`If-Modified-Since` with `304`.
The domain is registered in the site owner's name and account, with 2FA, auto-renew and registrar lock. Credentials live in a shared password vault.

A CAA record limits certificate issuers. DNSSEC is on where the registrar supports it. All name servers return the right A/CNAME records (changes take up to 72 h). Lower TTLs to a few hours or less at least 7 days before a DNS migration.
verify: `dig CAA`; `dig` per name server; DNSSEC analyzer

rule: Every domain that sends email has SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Start DMARC at `p=none` with reports, then move to `quarantine` and `reject`.
Transactional email (forms, orders) goes through a dedicated provider on its own subdomain, with aligned SPF/DKIM.
verify: Header check of a test email

rule: Transactional emails (confirmations, orders, password resets): HTML plus a plain-text part, one column ≤ 600 px, live text instead of images, `lang` set, layout tables with `role="presentation"`, alt text, body text ≥ 16 px, absolute links with descriptive text, token colors that pass A11Y-07, and a logo that works in dark mode. The sender name is consistent and replies reach a monitored inbox. No marketing content or tracking without a legal basis (PRV-01). Tested in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail, light and dark.

Marketing email follows Gmail's sender guidelines: aligned SPF, DKIM and DMARC (TEC-15), valid forward and reverse DNS, TLS, one-click unsubscribe (`List-Unsubscribe` with an HTTPS URI plus `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`, both covered by DKIM, RFC 8058) and a visible unsubscribe link in the body, honored within 48 hours, and a user-reported spam rate below 0.3 % in Postmaster Tools (aim below 0.1 %). Gmail enforces the unsubscribe and DMARC parts for bulk senders (about 5,000 messages a day to Gmail); follow them at any volume. Consent per PRV-11.
Forms validate on the server and show clear success and error states. Delivery is confirmed by a test submission.

Spam protection without tracking: honeypot, time trap and rate limit first; a privacy-friendly challenge if spam persists, and from the start on open sign-up forms (accounts, user content). Never a puzzle-only CAPTCHA (see A11Y-20).
The CMS content model has structured fields for title, meta description, slug, social image, alt text (required), author and dates, plus drafts, preview, versions and roles.

Every external script, embed, font or pixel is listed in the third-party inventory in [`project-brief.md`](../templates/project-brief.md): purpose, owner, consent category, data shared, performance cost, CSP origins. The default answer is no.

Map, social and secondary video embeds load as click-to-load placeholders until the user interacts or consents. Videos meant to rank (SEO-45) keep their player element in the HTML without user action (a click or consent gate is a user action): self-host with `<video>`, `poster` and `preload="none"`, or use an iframe with `loading="lazy"`.
verify: Network panel before interaction; URL Inspection for ranking videos

rule: API calls run on the server with timeouts, retries with backoff, a fallback UI and failure monitoring.

The CMS enforces on publish: title, meta description and alt text, or an explicit "decorative" flag (SEO-58); slug rules (SEO-12); minimum image sizes (SEO-19). A slug change creates a 301 automatically (SEO-09). Rich text allows only semantic elements (H2–H4, lists, links, tables with headers); no raw HTML, inline styles or colors outside the tokens (DES-11).
verify: Try to publish an incomplete page; change a slug

rule: Editorial workflow: roles with least privilege (author, editor, publisher, admin), an approval step for YMYL and legal pages (CON-11), scheduled publishing, and revision history with restore. Publishes feed the change log (MSR-26).

Editors build pages from library blocks (CMP-01) within constraints: section order per page type (LAY-14), one hero, one primary call to action (UX-06). Each block has help text and character limits that match its component's content limits.
verify: Build a test page in the CMS

rule: Handover includes editor training (TEC-27): a short guide per content type, the style guide (CON-17), the AI-writing checklist (CON-16), and image preparation (formats, sizes, alt text).

*(CMS)* Unpublished, scheduled, private and deleted content is absent from sitemaps, feeds, site search and CMS REST or GraphQL listings. A preview link opens one item only and needs login or an expiring unguessable token. Exports and backups download only for named roles.
verify: Search sitemap, RSS, API (`?status=draft`) and site search for a known draft slug unauthenticated; reuse item A's preview token on item B

rule: Code is in version control with a protected main branch, reviewed pull requests and CI on every pull request ([`ci/quality.yml`](../templates/ci/quality.yml)).
Use a formatter and a linter with default settings, one package manager, a lockfile (SEC-14) and `.editorconfig`.

Code comments explain why, not what: no banner or separator comments, step narration (`// Step 1`), end-of-block markers, doc blocks that only repeat the signature, or emoji; every `TODO` names an owner or issue.
No end-of-life runtime, framework, CMS or plugin in production. Dependency updates are automated and merged at least monthly.
The site repository has a README (run, build, deploy, rollback, owners) and an `AGENTS.md` ([template](../templates/AGENTS.md)).
Handover package: who has access to what, credentials in the vault, runbook, and licenses for fonts, images and code.
[house] Core Web Vitals are "good" at the 75th percentile of real users, on mobile and on desktop: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1.
verify: PageSpeed Insights field data; GSC Core Web Vitals (≈ 28 days after launch)

rule: Before launch, every key template passes in the lab: Lighthouse mobile, median of ≥ 3 runs, LCP ≤ 2.5 s, TBT ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1.

[house] PageSpeed Insights ([pagespeed.web.dev](https://pagespeed.web.dev)) scores ≥ 90 in all four categories (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO) on both Mobile and Desktop for every key template.
[house] Budgets per page: ≤ 1.5 MB transferred (landing pages ≤ 500 KB), ≤ 170 KB compressed JavaScript on content pages. TTFB ≤ 0.8 s (web.dev's "good" threshold), measured at p75 in CrUX.
Real-user Core Web Vitals are collected per template (web-vitals library → analytics or RUM tool).
No HTML, CSS or JS file exceeds 2 MB uncompressed: Googlebot reads only the first 2 MB of each file (64 MB for PDFs) and ignores the rest.
verify: Crawler file-size report; DevTools uncompressed size

rule: Images are AVIF or WebP (`<picture>` fallback if needed), resized to their display size with `srcset`/`sizes`, and compressed.
Every ``, `
The LCP image is in the initial HTML, never lazy-loaded, with `fetchpriority="high"`. Below-the-fold images use `loading="lazy"` (SEO-40).

No autoplaying hero video on mobile. Videos use a poster image and `preload="none"`. Secondary third-party players load as placeholders (TEC-21); videos meant to rank do not wait for a click (SEO-45).
No animated GIF or APNG: use `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline>` (MP4/WebM) or animated AVIF/WebP, with a poster that shows under reduced motion and when autoplay is blocked.
Fonts are WOFF2 ([house] self-hosted, which also avoids a third-party request, PRV-07), subset to the scripts in use, and limited to the weights in use (one variable font beats several static files).
`font-display: swap` or `optional`, with a metric-matched fallback (`size-adjust`, `ascent-override`). [house] Preload at most the 1–2 fonts used above the fold.
Scripts use `defer` or `type="module"`. No render-blocking third-party scripts in `<head>`.
Third-party scripts load only after consent or on interaction, and only those listed in the inventory (TEC-20).
JavaScript is split per route. Only interactive components hydrate. Unused JS and CSS are removed.
Interactions run no long tasks over 50 ms. Long work is split and yields to the main thread.

Scripts never interleave layout reads (`getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetHeight`, `scrollTop`) with style writes; script animation runs on `requestAnimationFrame`, the Web Animations API or CSS, never `setInterval`/`setTimeout`; pure computation over 50 ms moves to a Web Worker.
`will-change` is set only on an element about to animate and removed afterwards, never in a global or `*` rule.

Key templates stay under 1,400 DOM nodes (Lighthouse warns from about 800); long off-screen sections use `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size`; in-app lists over 100 rows are windowed or paginated (CMP-18).
Pages qualify for the back/forward cache: no `unload` handlers and no `Cache-Control: no-store` on public pages.
Fingerprinted static assets send `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. HTML is revalidated (`no-cache` or short `max-age`).
`preconnect` only to critical third-party origins (≤ 2, Lighthouse warns above that). No unused preloads.
Multi-page sites prerender likely next pages with Speculation Rules (`moderate` eagerness).
verify: DevTools → Application → Background services → Speculative loads

rule: Cross-document View Transitions are added as progressive enhancement: same-origin, crossfade ≤ 300 ms from the motion tokens, off under `prefers-reduced-motion`, render-blocking for at most one critical element, and lab LCP compared with and without them ([house]).
Page weight and request count are tracked as a proxy for energy use. Static, cached delivery is preferred.

⚗ Sustainable delivery (W3C Web Sustainability Guidelines, draft): hosting runs on verified renewable energy (Green Web Foundation check or the provider's published report); video does not autoplay by default (PRF-09) and users control playback and resolution. [house] Hosting sits in a region close to the audience, video streams adaptively, and unused pages, media, fonts and third-party scripts are removed at least yearly (TEC-20).
verify: Green Web check; yearly cleanup record

rule: ⚗ The CO₂ estimate per page view of each key template is calculated with the Sustainable Web Design Model (e.g. CO2.js), recorded with PRF-21, and does not rise between releases.
Conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA. WCAG 2.2 is ISO/IEC 40500:2025, and the EU standard EN 301 549 is moving to it. WCAG 3 is a draft, not a target.

[EU] B2C e-commerce services (Germany: BFSG, in force since 28 Jun 2025) must comply and publish an accessibility statement with a feedback contact. Exempt: service providers with < 10 employees **and** ≤ €2 m annual turnover or balance sheet. Sites outside that scope SHOULD publish a statement too.
Use landmarks (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `footer`) with exactly one `main`. The first focusable element is a skip link to the main content.

Headings form a logical outline with no skipped levels. Lists, tables (`th` with `scope`), buttons and links use native elements. ARIA only where no native element exists, following the ARIA Authoring Practices.
`lang` is set on `<html>` and on inline passages in another language.
Informative images have meaningful `alt` text; decorative images have `alt=""`. Icon-only controls have accessible names. Charts and diagrams have a text equivalent.
Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1, large text ≥ 3:1, UI components and focus indicators ≥ 3:1. Color is never the only carrier of meaning.
verify: Contrast checker on tokens and screens

rule: Content reflows at 320 CSS px and 200 % zoom without loss or 2-D scrolling (data tables and maps excepted). Text-spacing overrides don't break the layout. Zoom is never disabled.
Videos have captions and audio has transcripts. No audio autoplays. Anything that moves for more than 5 s can be paused.
Animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second.

The reduced-motion variant removes movement, not feedback: no translate, scale, rotate, zoom or parallax, no autoplaying background video or looping decoration, `scroll-behavior: auto`, infinite spinners replaced by a static or text status; opacity and color cross-fades ≤ 150 ms stay so state changes remain visible (WCAG 2.3.3).
verify: OS setting or emulation: `document.getAnimations()` holds no transform animations; hover, focus and dialog still change visibly

rule: *(keyboard shortcuts)* Single-character shortcuts can be turned off, remapped or work only on focus (WCAG 2.1.4). Handlers match `event.key` for characters, so they work on non-QWERTY layouts, and show the platform modifier (⌘ or Ctrl).
verify: Test with an AZERTY layout; turn shortcuts off

rule: Everything works by keyboard alone, in a logical order, with no keyboard traps.
Every focusable element shows a visible focus indicator. Sticky headers, chat widgets and cookie banners never hide the focused element entirely (2.4.11).
Targets are at least 24 × 24 CSS px or have enough spacing (2.5.8). Touch-target size for primary controls: LAY-08.
Every drag interaction has a single-pointer alternative (2.5.7).
Link and button text makes sense in context. No "click here" or "read more" without an accessible name that says what.
Form fields have visible labels that are programmatically associated. Required fields and formats are stated in text. Personal-data fields use `autocomplete`.
Errors are shown in text next to the field, with a suggestion for fixing them. Status messages are announced through live regions.
verify: Screen reader test of failed submit

rule: No redundant entry: data already given in a process is auto-filled or offered for selection (3.3.7).
Help (contact, chat, FAQ) appears in the same relative place on every page (3.2.6).
Accessible authentication: no cognitive test (puzzle, character transcription) without an alternative. Pasting and password managers are allowed (3.3.8).
Use plain language. Expand abbreviations on first use. Keep labels and navigation consistent.
Run accessibility checks in component tests and end-to-end tests, not only on finished pages.
An automated axe-based scan shows 0 violations on every template in CI. Automated tools catch only some issues, so A11Y-24 still applies.
Key flows are tested manually: keyboard only, a screen reader (NVDA + Chrome or Firefox; VoiceOver + Safari on macOS and iOS), 200 % zoom and the mobile screen reader.
People with disabilities take part in usability tests of core flows.
HTTPS only. TLS 1.3 is enabled, TLS 1.2 (ECDHE suites) is the minimum, and SSL, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are off.
`Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`, once every subdomain serves HTTPS.

Baseline headers: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, a `Permissions-Policy` that denies unused features, `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` for legacy browsers. Template: [`_headers`](../templates/_headers).

Send `Content-Security-Policy` as an HTTP header, not `<meta>`. Minimum: `default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests`. Roll it out with `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` first.
Strict script CSP: nonces or hashes plus `'strict-dynamic'`. No `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts. Violations are reported via `report-to`.
Hide server version and `X-Powered-By`. Don't send `X-XSS-Protection` (obsolete). No public directory listings, `.git`, `.env`, backups or private source maps.
Add the domain to the HSTS preload list. Use COEP `require-corp` and CORP `same-origin` where no cross-origin embeds are needed.
Cookies are `Secure`, `HttpOnly` unless scripts must read them, and `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict`. Session cookies use the `__Host-` prefix and a short lifetime.
No `eval` or `new Function`. Untrusted data never goes into `innerHTML` or `document.write`. Output is encoded for its context with the framework's escaping.
Every form and API validates input on the server and uses parameterized queries. Uploads are checked against an allowlist of type and size, stored outside the web root, and SVG is denied by default.
Access control runs on the server for every request and action. Admin and CMS logins require MFA and are rate-limited. No default credentials.
State-changing requests are protected against CSRF (SameSite cookies plus a token for authenticated actions) and are rate-limited.

If the site has user accounts, follow NIST SP 800-63B-4: passwords ≥ 15 characters without MFA or ≥ 8 with MFA, maximum ≥ 64, no composition rules, no forced rotation. Check against breached-password lists, hash with Argon2id, give generic login errors and offer MFA.
Supply chain (OWASP A03): committed lockfile, frozen installs in CI, dependency vulnerability scan and secret scan in CI, 2FA on Git, registry, hosting and DNS accounts.

Critical security patches for CMS, plugins and runtime ship within 48 hours, all others within 7 days. Every CMS, plugin, forum and blog (even forgotten ones) is inventoried with its version. Servers are reached by SSH/SFTP, never FTP or telnet.
Third-party scripts are self-hosted or pinned with Subresource Integrity.
Errors fail closed and never expose stack traces. Security events (logins, admin changes) are logged without unnecessary personal data and alert on anomalies.
Publish `/.well-known/security.txt` (RFC 9116) with `Contact` and an `Expires` date less than a year ahead. Template: [`security.txt`](../templates/security.txt).
Before launch, a DAST baseline scan (e.g. ZAP) shows no high-risk findings.

Hack detection: Search Console messages are forwarded to a monitored mailbox, the Security issues and Manual actions reports stay clean, and `site:example.com` plus spam terms (e.g. `casino`) is checked monthly for injected pages. Logs are watched for open-redirect abuse (`=http:` or `=//` parameters, spikes on redirect URLs).
verify: GSC Security issues; `site:` query; log review

rule: Incident runbook for a flagged site: review the Search Console owner list for unknown owners, open the flagged sample URLs from a machine outside the site's network and refresh several times, fix every cause, then request one review. Never toggle between clean and compromised states (Safe Browsing Repeat Offenders get no review requests for 30 days).

Embedded ads and third-party components are vetted: deceptive ads or pop-up redirects count against the host page. Hosted payment, booking or login pages run by a third party show that party's brand on every page and state the relationship (social-engineering flag).

*(server fetches)* Server-side fetches of user-influenced URLs (link previews, imports, webhook targets) allow only `https` to allowlisted hosts, block loopback, private and link-local ranges (incl. `169.254.169.254` and IPv6) after DNS resolution, re-check every redirect hop and cap time and size.
verify: Submit `http://127.0.0.1`, the metadata IP, a name resolving to `10.0.0.1` and redirects to each: all rejected

rule: Redirect targets from `next`, `return` or `url` parameters are relative paths or exact allowlisted hosts; `//`, `\`, `javascript:` and foreign URLs are rejected. CR/LF from request data never reaches a response header.

*(CORS)* `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is an exact allowlist, never reflected from `Origin` and never `null`. Credentials only with one named origin; per-user responses never use `*`; dynamic values send `Vary: Origin`.
verify: `curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://evil.example'` and `Origin: null` per API route: no ACAO

rule: *(files)* Paths built from request data are canonicalized and confined to a base directory; stored files get server-generated names; archive extraction rejects entries outside the target.

*(uploads)* Extends SEC-10: type is detected from the file's bytes, not its name or `Content-Type`. Uploads are served with `nosniff` and `Content-Disposition: attachment` or from a separate cookieless origin; images are re-encoded with pixel and decompressed-size limits.
verify: Upload HTML renamed `.jpg`, `shell.php.jpg`, a 50,000 × 50,000 px PNG: none renders inline or runs, the large image is refused

rule: Request data never reaches a shell, template compiler, XML parser with external entities or a native deserializer (`unserialize`, `pickle`). Subprocesses take argument arrays; NoSQL and LDAP filters are built from typed fields.
verify: SAST plus review; `;id`, `{{7*7}}` and an XXE document stay inert

rule: Absolute URLs in emails, redirects, canonicals and sitemaps come from a configured base URL, never from `Host`, `X-Forwarded-Host` or `Forwarded`. The app answers only for its own hostnames.
verify: `curl -H 'Host: evil.example'` and `X-Forwarded-Host` on pages, redirects and the reset email: value absent or rejected

rule: *(accounts, personalized pages)* Per-user responses send `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. The CDN cache key includes every input that changes the response; static-asset rules never match dynamic paths (`/account/x.css`, `/account;a.js`). Public pages keep PRF-16.
verify: Logged in, request those paths; fetch anonymously elsewhere: no private content, no cache HIT

rule: *(accounts)* A new session ID on login, privilege change and MFA; sessions invalidated server-side on logout, password change and account disable; IDs from a CSPRNG with ≥ 64 bits of entropy; idle and absolute timeouts; logout clears client-side private data.
verify: Cookie changes after login; the old cookie returns 401 after logout or password change

rule: *(accounts)* Reset, invite, email-change and magic-link tokens are random, single-use, short-lived, bound to one account and action, and stored hashed. A reset revokes other sessions. Login, reset and sign-up answer identically, in content and timing, for known and unknown accounts.
verify: Reuse, expiry and cross-account tests; compare responses for a known vs. unknown email

rule: *(JWT, OAuth, OIDC)* The server pins the JWT algorithm and key source and checks `iss`, `aud` and `exp`; header-chosen `jku`/`kid` are not trusted. Clients bind `state` and PKCE to the session and check the ID-token `nonce`; `redirect_uri` matches exactly.
verify: `alg=none`, wrong `aud`, expired token, foreign `state`, `redirect_uri` variant: all rejected

rule: Extends SEC-11: every route that takes an object ID checks the caller's right to that object (read, update, delete, list, export, bulk, file download). Writes accept an allowlist of fields, so `role`, `owner`, `price` and `status` can't be set from the request.
verify: As user A, request user B's IDs on every verb; send `role=admin`: 403/404, nothing changes

rule: *(webhooks)* Inbound webhooks verify the provider's signature over the raw body with a constant-time compare and a timestamp tolerance, reject replayed event IDs, and take account and event type only from the verified payload.
verify: Unsigned, wrongly signed, stale and replayed posts: 4xx, no side effect

rule: Production has debug mode off with no switch via parameter or header. Unauthenticated `/debug`, `/phpinfo.php`, `/server-status`, `/actuator`, `/metrics`, GraphQL introspection (unless public) and CMS user-listing endpoints return 401, 403 or 404; seed and sample accounts are removed.
verify: Probe the list on production; try `?debug=1`

rule: Extends SEC-09: user or CMS HTML is sanitized with an allowlist sanitizer on output (Trusted Types where supported). `href`, `src`, `location` and `window.open` values from requests, fragments or storage are `https:`, `mailto:` or relative, never `javascript:` or `data:`.
verify: Submit `` and a `javascript:` link: both render inert

rule: *(postMessage, WebSockets)* Message handlers check `event.origin` against an exact allowlist; sensitive messages never target `"*"`. WebSocket upgrades check `Origin`, authenticate with a per-connection token (not cookies alone) and re-authorize each message.
verify: Post from an unlisted origin; connect with `Origin: https://evil.example`: ignored or 403

rule: Recursive merge or path-assign on request data rejects `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype`, or uses `Map`/`Object.create(null)`.

*(service worker)* The worker is same-origin at the narrowest scope and never caches responses with `Authorization`, `Set-Cookie`, `private` or `no-store`; logout and account switches purge its caches.
verify: DevTools → Application → Cache Storage after login, logout and switch

rule: Request body size is capped (≤ 1 MB by default, uploads per SEC-10), list endpoints cap `limit` and query depth, every server-side call has a timeout, user-supplied regexes never run, and limits apply before expensive work.
verify: 10 MB body → 413; `?limit=100000` capped; a ReDoS probe stays fast

rule: CI hardening: workflows running pull-request code get `contents: read` and no secrets; no PR checkout under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` with secrets; third-party actions pinned to a full commit SHA; event fields (branch, title) never interpolated into `run:`; no unpinned `curl \| sh` or `npx` without a version.

Dependency confusion and install scripts: scoped internal package names, the registry pinned in a committed `.npmrc`, install scripts of new dependencies reviewed or CI on `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, lockfile integrity verified. Extends SEC-14.
verify: Registry config and CI install step review

rule: *(accounts)* Fetch Metadata: authenticated apps reject non-navigation requests with `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` as defense in depth against CSRF and cross-site leaks.
Origin servers, databases, admin panels and management ports are unreachable from the internet except through the CDN or WAF, an allowlist or a VPN; requests that bypass the CDN are refused.
verify: Port scan of the own origin (with approval): only 80/443; `curl --resolve host:443:<origin-ip>` refused

rule: *(shop, forms with prices)* The server recomputes price, discount, shipping, tax and totals from catalog data and ignores client-sent prices, roles and currencies; negative, zero or fractional quantities are rejected; orders, coupons and sign-ups are atomic, and steps can't be skipped.
verify: Tamper price and `qty=-1`; 20 parallel coupon redeems → one success; open the confirmation URL directly

rule: [EU] Before consent, nothing non-essential is stored on or read from the device (cookies, storage, fingerprinting), and no third-party request sends personal data (TDDDG §25, GDPR).
verify: Fresh profile: network and storage before consent

rule: [EU] The consent banner shows accept and reject with equal prominence on the first layer. Purposes are granular, nothing is pre-ticked, there is no consent wall, withdrawal is as easy as consent (persistent link), and consent is logged.
verify: Banner review against the DSK guidance

rule: Google tags run only with Consent Mode v2: `ad_storage`, `analytics_storage`, `ad_user_data` and `ad_personalization` default to `denied` before any tag fires, and the CMP updates them. Sites showing Google ads need a Google-certified CMP. Template: [`consent-default.html`](../templates/consent-default.html).

[EU] A privacy policy is linked from every page. It names the controller, the DPO if required, purposes and legal bases, every recipient, third-country transfers and their safeguards, retention periods, data subject rights and the right to complain.

[EU] Every processor (hosting, analytics, forms, email, CMP) has a data processing agreement (Art. 28 GDPR). US recipients must be certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or covered by standard contractual clauses plus a transfer impact assessment.
Collect only the data each purpose needs. Retention periods are defined and enforced automatically. Logs are anonymized or short-lived.
Privacy-friendly defaults: fonts per PRF-10, click-to-load embeds (TEC-21), and cookieless analytics where it suffices. Whether consent is still needed is assessed legally.
[EU] Keep a record of processing activities (Art. 30). Run a DPIA where required. Have a breach process that can notify within 72 hours.
Outside the EU: honor Global Privacy Control. Add a CCPA/CPRA "Do Not Sell or Share" link if in scope. UK GDPR/PECR mirror the EU rules. Check local law for each target market.

[EU] Germany: an Impressum per DDG §5, labelled "Impressum" and reachable from every page. It gives name and address, legal form and representatives, email plus another fast contact, register and number, VAT ID, and the supervisory authority, chamber and professional rules for regulated professions.
Newsletters use double opt-in, keep a consent record (time and text version) and include an unsubscribe link in every email.

[EU] E-commerce must provide: pre-contract information, withdrawal policy, total prices including VAT and shipping (PAngV), an order button labelled "zahlungspflichtig bestellen" or equivalent (§312j BGB), a cancellation button for B2C subscriptions (§312k BGB) and a consumer-arbitration statement (VSBG §36). The EU ODR-platform link is no longer required since 20 Jul 2025.

[EU] AI Act Art. 50 (applies since 2 Aug 2026): tell users when they are talking to an AI system. Label AI-generated or manipulated images, audio and video (deepfakes), and AI-generated text published to inform the public unless it was human-reviewed under editorial responsibility.
[house] A Search Console **Domain property** is verified by DNS TXT before launch. At least two people are owners, one of them the site owner.
[house] The XML sitemap is submitted in Search Console, and the Page indexing report shows no key URL excluded unexpectedly.
On launch day, the home page and top money pages are checked with URL Inspection and indexing is requested for them. Everything else gets indexed through the sitemap and accurate `lastmod`.
Bing Webmaster Tools is verified (import from Search Console) with the sitemap submitted. An IndexNow key is hosted, and new or changed URLs are submitted automatically.
Search Console and Bing email alerts are on, and Search Console messages are forwarded to a monitored mailbox. Search Console is linked to GA4.

Search Console keeps only 16 months of data: bulk export to BigQuery (or the API) is on. Every significant title, content, template or migration change is logged with its date so traffic changes can be attributed.
verify: GSC bulk export link; change log

rule: After the first deploy and after every template release, the matching Search Console reports are checked: Rich result status (valid up, invalid not up), Unparsable structured data, Merchant listings and Product snippets (shops), Video indexing (video sites), Manual actions. Fixes are validated there.

Quarterly (monthly for large sites; house heuristic), Crawl stats (host availability, `5xx`, response time) is read together with Page indexing, and the Google-selected canonical of key URLs is compared with the declared one.

Search Console access: agencies, freelancers and tools get Full or Restricted permission, never Owner; delegated owners come only from the site owner's staff. Leavers are removed on their last day, and access is reviewed quarterly. The site owner's verification token (DNS TXT) stays in place; a leaver's own tokens are deleted under Users and permissions → Unused ownership tokens. Only owners can submit sitemaps, so the site owner submits them (MSR-32).
verify: GSC → Settings → Users and permissions; DNS lookup

rule: Sitemaps report: the sitemap index (or each sitemap) is submitted once per property and shows "Success". Discovered URLs roughly match the indexable URLs in `url-map.csv`, and the Page indexing view filtered by sitemap shows key URLs indexed. No resubmitting or pinging after updates (Google retired the ping endpoint); accurate `lastmod` is enough (SEO-07).

The robots.txt report (Settings) lists each host's file (a Domain property shows the top 20 hosts) as "Fetched" with a recent "Checked on" date. After an urgent robots.txt fix, request a recrawl there (SEO-03, SEO-38).

Page indexing triage (extends MSR-02): every reason under "Why pages aren't indexed" is classified. Intended: URL marked 'noindex', page with redirect, alternate page with proper canonical, not found for removed URLs. Defect: soft 404, server error (5xx), URL blocked by robots.txt on a wanted URL, "Crawled/Discovered – currently not indexed" or "Duplicate without user-selected canonical" on a key URL. Defects are diagnosed in URL Inspection (indexed vs. live test, rendered HTML and screenshot, smartphone crawler, declared vs. Google-selected canonical), fixed, and closed with "Validate Fix" until it shows "Passed".

Manual actions and Security issues are checked weekly (SEC-20). On a finding: fix every affected page against the named policy, then select "Request Review" in the report and submit a reconsideration request stating the problem, the fix and the evidence. Log the case with its dates (MSR-26).
verify: GSC Manual actions; Security issues; case log

rule: Monthly Performance review: brand vs. non-brand split (regex filter on brand terms, or the branded-queries filter where available); queries at positions 4–20 with CTR below the site's median for that position, sent to title and snippet work (SEO-15, SEO-61); the pages and queries losing the most clicks against the previous period; each search type (Web, Image, Video, News) plus Discover; search appearance filters. The Core Web Vitals and HTTPS reports show no Poor or non-HTTPS URLs (PRF-01, SEC-01).
verify: GSC Performance; Core Web Vitals; HTTPS

rule: Quarterly Links report: every key page appears among internally linked pages, with link counts that reflect its importance (SEO-22, SEO-23); top linking sites and anchor texts are reviewed with SEO-28. Associations are in place: GA4 (MSR-05), Merchant Center for shops, Google Ads where used.
A measurement plan exists before implementation: business goals → KPIs → key events → parameters ([`project-brief.md`](../templates/project-brief.md)).
If GA4 is used: setup with data retention 14 months, internal and developer traffic filtered, unwanted referrals excluded, cross-domain measurement where needed, correct time zone and currency.
Every primary conversion (successful form submit, purchase, sign-up, call click) is a key event and has been tested in DebugView.
Enhanced measurement is reviewed: keep page views, scrolls, outbound clicks, downloads and site search. Turn off form interactions if they misfire, and replace them with custom events.
Events and parameters follow a documented naming convention (`snake_case`, `verb_object`).
E-commerce uses the recommended GA4 events (`view_item` → `purchase`) with a unique `transaction_id`.
BigQuery export is on for raw-data ownership and history beyond the retention limit.
Without Google Ads, privacy-friendly analytics (EU-hosted or self-hosted, cookieless) is considered. The consent requirement is assessed legally (PRV-07).

Search Console is the source of truth for search performance, GA4 for on-site behavior. The organic dashboard pairs GSC clicks with GA4 sessions (source `google`, medium `organic`) under identical country and device filters and compares trend shape, not totals (GSC uses Pacific Time, counts canonical URLs only and ignores consent; GA4 depends on its tag and opt-outs).
verify: Looker Studio or GA4 vs. GSC

rule: If marketing or Google tags are used: all tags run through one tag manager container owned by the site owner. No duplicate hard-coded tags.

Every tag has consent settings. Basic Consent Mode (tags load after consent) is the default; advanced mode needs a documented legal assessment. A test shows no Google request that sets or reads cookies before consent (PRV-03).
Use one workspace per change and named versions with notes. Test in preview before publishing. [house] At most 3 people can publish.
A UTM convention (lowercase, fixed vocabulary for `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`) is used for all campaigns, never on internal links.
Server-side tagging on a first-party subdomain controls what data reaches vendors.
Ads conversions are imported from GA4 key events, or use the Ads tag with enhanced conversions. Both are consent-gated.

[house] E-commerce: Merchant Center gets its product feed by file, a platform integration or the Merchant API, never the sunset Content API for Shopping. Feed, on-page `Product` markup and the visible page agree on price, currency, availability and condition. Free listings are opted in, and Merchant Center updates price and availability automatically from the website when they differ.
Uptime monitoring runs every ≤ 5 minutes with a keyword check on the home page and one key page. Alerts go to ≥ 2 people or channels.
Expiry alerts at least 30 days ahead for TLS certificates, domain registration and the `security.txt` `Expires` date.
JavaScript and server errors are tracked with alerting. Source maps are uploaded privately.

Real-user Core Web Vitals per template (PRF-05) and rankings for the core keyword set (from `url-map.csv`) are tracked weekly, by device and market. Rank data comes from Search Console or a licensed provider, never from automated queries to Google.
One KPI dashboard is reviewed monthly. It covers sessions by channel, key events, conversion rate, organic clicks and impressions, Core Web Vitals and AI visibility.

Traffic-drop triage order: check Search Console Data anomalies and Google's ranking-updates list; view the last 16 months (seasonality); split by search type, device and country; stable impressions with fewer clicks means a title or snippet problem; compare the query in Google Trends. After a core update, wait a full week after rollout ends and compare with the week before it began. Leave pages that lost only a few positions (2 to 4) unchanged.

Each language or market has its own URL. Default: subdirectories (`/de/`, `/en/`). Use ccTLDs only with a strong local presence (house choices: subdirectory default, ccTLD limit). Never select the language by cookie, parameter or IP alone.
No automatic redirects by IP or `Accept-Language`. A visible switcher links to the equivalent page in the other language, not to its home page.
verify: Test with a VPN and with browser language changed

rule: hreflang: every version lists all versions including itself, reciprocally, with absolute URLs and `x-default`. Codes are ISO 639-1 language, optionally with an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region (`de-AT`; not `en-UK`, `es-419`, `EU` or a region alone; `zh-Hans` is fine). Several locales of one language also get a generic language URL (`en`). In HTML, tags sit in a well-formed `<head>`, one per version, with no other attributes such as `media`. Use one method only: HTML, HTTP header or sitemap. Template: [`head.html`](../templates/head.html).

Each language version is self-canonical. Never canonicalize across languages. Same-language regional variants with near-identical body text (`en-US`/`en-GB`; `example.de/` vs. `example.com/de/`) are duplicates: choose a preferred URL, canonicalize to it and keep hreflang.
The `lang` attribute matches the content language (A11Y-05), and `og:locale` is set.

Everything is localized: navigation, UI text, title and description, alt text, structured data, error pages and legal pages. No mixed-language pages: one language per page for content and navigation, no side-by-side translations. The `<title>` uses the page's language and script (no transliteration).
Localize rather than translate: keyword research per market, local examples, currency, units, payment methods, phone formats and trust signals, reviewed by a native speaker.
Dates, numbers, currencies, units and lists are formatted per locale with the `Intl` APIs. Time zones are explicit.
Plurals go through `Intl.PluralRules` or ICU messages, never `count + "s"`; UI strings are complete messages with named variables, not concatenated fragments.
verify: Grep; pseudo-locale with Arabic and Polish plural forms

rule: Brand and product names, code and identifiers that must stay literal carry `translate="no"` on that element, never on the whole page.
verify: Chrome Translate on a page: those strings stay unchanged

rule: Layouts tolerate 30–40 % longer text and other scripts (font subsets per script, PRF-10).

Right-to-left languages use `dir="rtl"` on `<html>`, CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, not `margin-left`), mirrored directional icons, and `<bdi>` or `dir="auto"` to isolate mixed-direction text.
Source strings live outside the templates, with a translation memory and glossary. Machine translation is never published without human review (CON-09).
Search performance and rankings are reviewed per language folder and market (MSR-24).
Markets with a physical presence get their own local entity signals: Business Profile, local phone and address.

Country targeting uses URL structure and hreflang. Page language is read from visible content, not `lang`, hreflang or the URL. `.io`, `.co`, `.ai`, `.me`, `.tv`, `.eu`, `.asia` and other generic TLDs do not geotarget. `geo.position` and `distribution` meta tags are ignored.
verify: URL map; GSC page filter per folder

rule: robots.txt and robots meta are identical in every locale. Googlebot is never geo-blocked unless users from that country are blocked too (it crawls from US and non-US IPs). Locale-adaptive content is checked with URL Inspection.
Use Baseline "Widely available" web features freely, and newer features only with a fallback. Test the last 2 versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (macOS and iOS), plus Chrome on Android.
Test viewports 360, 390, 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 px: no overflow, overlap or clipped content (UX-05).
CI runs static checks on every change: HTML validation (TEC-02), lint and format (TEC-24), link check (SEO-25).
Lighthouse CI runs on key templates, median of 3 runs, with assertions for performance (PRF-02), accessibility (A11Y-23) and SEO. Failing assertions block the merge.

Every critical flow (contact, checkout, sign-up, login) has end-to-end tests in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Tests use role or label locators and test data, and never real endpoints that send email or take payment.
Key templates have visual regression snapshots taken in a pinned environment (fixed OS and browser image), reviewed on every UI change.
Before launch, test manually on a real iOS phone and a real Android phone, with throttled network (slow 4G) and CPU. The Back button returns to the previous page.
Before launch, crawl the full site: status codes, canonicals, titles, descriptions, H1, structured data, internal links, sitemap vs. crawl.

Content QA: no placeholder text (`lorem`, `TODO`, `example.com`, `XXX`, `REPLACE`), no empty ``, placeholder image hosts (`placehold`, `picsum`) or grey stand-in boxes, no sample names or numbers (`John Doe`, `Acme`, `Your Name`, `[X]`, `555-`, `123,456`), no `href="#"`, empty handlers or buttons without an action, no unbuilt features in the navigation, no indexable test pages, spelling checked, every link, phone number and email address works, legal pages final.
Defect severity: **P0** site down, legal or security breach. **P1** core flow broken or a MUST rule failing. **P2** SHOULD rule failing or noticeable issue. **P3** cosmetic. P0 and P1 block launch.
Definition of done for each change: the affected rule IDs are verified, CI is green, the preview is checked at 390 and 1440 px, and the console shows no errors.
Visual QA compares implementation and design at identical viewports and states, and records every deviation.
Dynamic endpoints are load-tested for the expected peak (e.g. a launch campaign).

Visual QA and screenshot tests run on the production build (`build` plus `preview`), not the dev server; screenshots are taken after entrance motion settles (or under reduced-motion emulation), full-page from the top, and each file is opened to confirm it is complete.
verify: Build command recorded in the PR; screenshot review

rule: Pre-launch security review: list every entry point (forms, APIs, uploads, auth routes, webhooks, redirects, admin, WebSockets) and tick each against SEC-08 to SEC-46; anything unreviewed is recorded as "not covered", never as passed. P0/P1 security findings are re-checked by a second person who tries to refute them.
verify: Attack-surface inventory in the audit report

rule: [house] The real-iPhone test (QA-07) includes Low Power Mode, which can suspend autoplay video and animation: the poster fallback shows and no content depends on motion.
verify: iPhone with Low Power Mode on

rule: Every page, component and flow is designed and reviewed against this file and standards 02, 03 and 09. When principles conflict, usability and accessibility win over aesthetics and persuasion.

Gestalt: related items sit closer together than unrelated ones (proximity, ≥ one φ step, DES-05); the same function looks the same (similarity); groups share a common region (card, background, border); elements share alignment lines (continuity); overlays and dialogs separate clearly from the page (figure-ground).

Visual hierarchy: each view has one focal point (headline or primary call to action). Importance is shown through size, weight, contrast, color and position. Text pages support F-pattern scanning (front-loaded headings, short paragraphs); landing sections follow a Z-pattern.
verify: Blur test: the focal point stays identifiable

rule: Hick's Law: few choices per decision. ≤ 7 top-level navigation items (UX-02), one primary action per view (UX-06), ≤ 4 pricing plans with one recommended, filters and advanced options behind progressive disclosure.

Fitts's Law: frequent and primary actions are large and close to the user's attention and thumb: touch targets per LAY-08, full-width primary buttons in mobile forms, primary actions within thumb reach on mobile, whole cards or rows clickable when they are one target. Destructive actions are smaller and placed away from the primary action.

Jakob's Law: follow conventions users know from other sites: logo top-left linking home, main navigation at the top (menu button on mobile), search and cart top-right, underlined text links, legal and contact links in the footer, standard icons. Deviate only with a tested benefit (UX-13).

Nielsen heuristics 1–5: system status is visible (feedback ≤ 100 ms, progress indicator for waits > 1 s); the site speaks the users' language (UX-01); users stay in control (undo, cancel, back, Esc closes dialogs); consistency and standards (DES-07, PSY-06); errors are prevented (constraints, sensible defaults, destructive or costly actions per UX-28).

Nielsen heuristics 6–10: recognition over recall (visible options, persistent labels, remembered input); flexibility and efficiency (autofill, shortcuts, saved progress); aesthetic and minimalist design (every element earns its place); errors explained in plain words with a fix (UX-15, A11Y-17); help available where needed (A11Y-19).

Cognitive load: chunk content and fields into groups of about 4; one main task per screen in flows; forms with more than about 7 fields become steps with a progress indicator; no competing animations, banners or pop-ups during a task; plain language (CON-08); explanations sit next to the point of use.
verify: Field and choice counts; task walkthrough

rule: Response time: every interaction is acknowledged within 100 ms and completes or shows progress within 400 ms (Doherty threshold). Use optimistic UI where it is safe; on failure it rolls back, shows the error and offers retry or Undo. Complements INP (PRF-01).

Attention and memory: the most important items come first or last in lists (serial position effect); the primary action looks distinct from everything else (isolation effect); the end of each journey (confirmation, thank-you, error) gets deliberate care (peak-end rule).

Social proof is real and verifiable: testimonials with full name, role and photo (with consent), ratings from third-party platforms with their source, customer counts and figures with source, date and baseline, logos with permission; no round filler ("10,000+") without evidence, placed near decisions (UX-08). Never fabricated or selectively edited (SEO-47).

Ethical conversion psychology: show the value before any ask; remove friction (UX-09); reverse risk with real guarantees and transparent prices; urgency, scarcity, reference prices and defaults must be true and in the user's interest (EU: discounts reference the lowest price of the previous 30 days). Test: the user would still agree after learning how the design works. No dark patterns (UX-11).

Evaluation: before launch and after major changes, at least 2 reviewers (3–5 where budget allows) run a heuristic evaluation of key flows against PSY-02 to PSY-13, each scoring independently (NN/g severity 0–4: 4 → P0/P1, 3 → P2, 1–2 → P3) before results are merged. Findings are rated with QA-10 severities; P0 and P1 are fixed before launch, the rest are tracked. Existing sites get the same audit first.
Tesler's Law: the system absorbs complexity: smart defaults, autofill (e.g. city from postcode), remembered choices, inline calculations instead of manual steps.
Aesthetic-usability effect: consistent spacing, alignment and typography raise perceived quality and trust. Polish never hides a usability problem found in testing.

Breakpoints are tokens for the four tiers above, written as mobile-first `min-width` media queries in `em` so they also follow the user's default font size (tokens hold px; the build emits `em`). Extra breakpoints only where content breaks (DES-16), never per device model.

Each tier uses the columns, gutters and outer margins from the table. Content never touches the viewport edge (≥ 16 px margin). Elements span whole columns and share alignment lines across sections (PSY-02).

Three content widths: prose ≤ 66 ch (≈ 680–720 px), wide 1200–1280 px (DES-16) and full-bleed for media and background bands only. Text never runs to full width on tablet, desktop or wide screens, and no line exceeds 75 ch at 1920 px.

Type scales per tier with `clamp()` built from `rem` plus `vw`, so text still enlarges at 200 % zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Body never drops below 16 px on any tier and may rise to 18 px on desktop. Headings step down per DES-04, tablets interpolate. Mobile keeps ≥ 35 ch per line.
Section padding follows the tier table. Card and grid gaps are 16 px on mobile and 26 px from tablet up. Control heights and component padding stay the same on every tier.

Layouts collapse in a predictable order: 61.8/38.2 splits stack once a column would fall below 320 px; card grids show 1 column on mobile, 2 on tablet, 3–4 on desktop (`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 280px), 1fr))`). Visual order equals DOM order on every tier; no `order` or `row-reverse` that breaks reading or focus order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
verify: Resize test; keyboard walkthrough per tier

rule: Reusable components (card, media object, teaser, widget) adapt to their container with container queries (`@container`); viewport media queries handle page layout only.
verify: CSS review; component in narrow and wide slot

rule: Input modality: hover effects only under `@media (any-hover: hover) and (any-pointer: fine)` (so trackpad tablets get them), sizing for touch under `(pointer: coarse)`, and every hover reveal has a tap and focus equivalent (UX-05). On coarse pointers, primary controls are ≥ 44 × 44 px with ≥ 8 px between adjacent targets (A11Y-13). Swipe and other path-based gestures always have a single-pointer button alternative (WCAG 2.5.1; drag: A11Y-14). Pinch zoom is never blocked by `touch-action` or the viewport tag (TEC-01, A11Y-08).
verify: Touch device test; DevTools pointer emulation

rule: Viewport and device: full-height areas use `svh`/`dvh` with a `vh` fallback; fixed and sticky bars respect `env(safe-area-inset-*)` (set `viewport-fit=cover` only when insets are handled). Portrait and landscape both work, with no orientation lock (WCAG 1.3.4). The on-screen keyboard never hides the focused field (no fixed bottom bar over inputs).
verify: iOS and Android device test in both orientations

rule: Tablets: test portrait 768–834 px and landscape 1024–1180 px. Don't infer touch from width: tablets with keyboard and trackpad get hover and focus styles too (LAY-08). Two-column layouts hold only while each column is ≥ 320 px.

Content parity: every tier carries the same content and functions (SEO-39). Smaller screens reorder (mobile-first DOM order) and condense (accordions, scrollable rows with a visible overflow cue) but never remove. At 360 × 640 the first screen shows the H1, the value proposition and the primary call to action (UX-07).
verify: Compare mobile and desktop DOM; screenshot at 360 × 640

rule: Responsive media: `srcset`/`sizes` match the layout width per tier (PRF-06); `<picture>` art direction when the subject would be too small on mobile; focal points kept with `object-position`; aspect-ratio tokens reserve space (PRF-07). No text baked into images; background images never carry content.
verify: Network panel per tier; screenshot review

rule: Tables, code blocks, charts and maps never cause page-level horizontal scrolling (UX-05, A11Y-08): they sit in a labelled, keyboard-focusable scroll container (`role="region"`, `aria-label`, `tabindex="0"`) or switch to a stacked layout below 600 px (CMP-04, WCAG 1.4.10).

Every text-bearing component is tested with stress fixtures: empty, one word, 3× average length, a 60-character unbroken string (URL, email, German compound), 0, 1 and 100+ items, emoji and an RTL string, at 320 px, 200 % zoom and with text-spacing overrides (WCAG 1.4.10, 1.4.12). Nothing overflows, overlaps or clips: flex and grid children set `min-width: 0`, user text `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, `line-clamp` only where CMP-01 sets a limit and the full text stays reachable.

Every template is built from fixed regions in this order: skip link → `header` → optional breadcrumbs (UX-03) → `main` with the H1 as its first heading → `footer` (A11Y-03). Each page type documents its section order in `DESIGN.md`, e.g. landing page: hero → problem and value → proof → offer or how it works → FAQ → final call to action. One section holds one idea under one H2.

Header: logo at the start linking home (PSY-06), primary navigation, utilities (search, language, account, cart), at most one call to action at the end, in the same order on every page (UX-02). Height ≤ 72 px on desktop, ≤ 64 px on mobile. If sticky, it hides on scroll down and returns on scroll up on mobile, and `scroll-padding-top` equals its height so anchors and focus stay visible (A11Y-12).
verify: Template review per tier; keyboard and anchor test

rule: Navigation per tier: from 1024 px, inline primary navigation; dropdowns and mega menus open on click, Enter and Space (hover optional) and follow the WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern. Below 1024 px, a labelled menu button (touch target per LAY-08, `aria-expanded`) opens a panel listing items in the desktop order. A modal drawer traps focus, closes with Esc and returns focus to the button. The current page has `aria-current="page"`. Apps may add a bottom tab bar of ≤ 5 items, each with icon and label.
verify: Keyboard and screen reader test per tier

rule: Hero: H1, a one-sentence value proposition and the primary call to action (at most one secondary) are visible without scrolling on every tier (UX-07); no avatar rows, chip rows or unsourced "trusted by" claims under them (PSY-12). Height is content-driven and never above 100 svh. Text over images passes A11Y-07 against the worst-case area (use a scrim). The hero image follows PRF-08.

Section rhythm: text/media splits alternate sides on desktop; on mobile, heading and text come before media unless the media is the content. Background bands use ≤ 2 surface tones, with no two full-bleed image bands in a row. Sections separate by spacing or a surface change, not both plus rules and shadows.
[house] Header, `main` and footer share one inline margin per tier, left equals right (±1 px), and a template has ≤ 4 distinct left edges for text blocks.
verify: Script collecting `getBoundingClientRect().left` of headings, text and media at 390 and 1440 px

rule: [house] Balance: from 1024 px no section leaves ≥ 40 % of its row empty, no background-only band is taller than 50 svh, and no empty block takes ≥ 28 % of the first viewport. No three sections in a row share one pattern (split, list, card grid, statement, full-bleed, table); a marketing page has ≤ 2 card grids.
verify: Screenshot scan at 1024 and 1440 px; section labels in the page blueprint

rule: [house] H1 runs ≤ 2 lines and ≤ about 12 words at 360, 768 and 1440 px; H2 ≤ 2 lines. Longer statements go in the lead paragraph.

Footer: brand and short claim, key navigation (UX-02), contact (UX-12) and a legal row that is never collapsed: Impressum (PRV-10), privacy policy (PRV-04), cookie settings (PRV-02), terms where applicable, copyright, plus language switch (I18N) and social links where they exist. 4–5 columns on desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on mobile (link groups may collapse into disclosures). Footer links meet LAY-08 on touch.

On mobile, all fixed and sticky elements together (header, call-to-action bar, chat launcher, banners) cover ≤ 25 % of the viewport height, and at most one sticky call-to-action bar exists. None hides the focused element (A11Y-12).
verify: Screenshot at 360 × 640 with all elements active

rule: With a fixed bottom bar, the page reserves `padding-bottom` and `scroll-padding-bottom` of at least the bar height plus the safe-area inset, so the last content and the focused control stay reachable (WCAG 2.4.11).
verify: Scroll to the end at 360 × 640; Tab to the last control

rule: Content pages (articles, docs, recipes, invoices) have a print stylesheet: navigation, banners and video hidden; dark text on white; external link URLs printed after the link; `break-inside: avoid` on figures and tables; `break-after: avoid` on headings.

Responsive QA: every template is checked at the QA-02 widths plus 320 px (WCAG 1.4.10), 844 × 390 (phone landscape) and 1180 × 820 (tablet landscape), and at 200 % zoom. Visual regression snapshots (QA-06) cover mobile, tablet and desktop.

Every component is specified in the library or `DESIGN.md`: anatomy, variants (≤ 3 sizes), tokens used, states (DES-06), behavior per tier (LAY-01), keyboard and ARIA behavior following the WAI-ARIA APG pattern where one exists, and content limits (e.g. title ≤ 2 lines).

Cards: one card shows one object. A clickable card has one real link (usually the title), stretched over the card with a pseudo-element, and no nested interactive elements inside that link. Fixed anatomy order: media → eyebrow → title (a heading at the right outline level) → text (≤ 3 lines) → meta → action. Cards in a row share equal height. Padding is 16 px on mobile and 26 px from tablet up, radius per DES-17, hover lift only under LAY-08, and a `:focus-within` ring.
verify: Component audit; keyboard and screen reader test

rule: Lists use native `ul`, `ol` or `dl` with hanging markers aligned to the text and item spacing per DES-25. Link lists keep rows ≥ 24 px (touch: LAY-08). Visible lists longer than 7 items are grouped under subheadings.

Tables hold data only, never layout. They have a `<caption>` or label and `th` with `scope` (A11Y-04). Text aligns to the start, numbers to the end with tabular numerals (DES-26). Long tables keep the header row sticky, use zebra stripes or dividers (not both), and touch-target rows (LAY-08). Sortable column headers wrap a button in the `th`; the `th` of the currently sorted column carries `aria-sort`. Below 600 px, use a scroll container with a sticky first column, or stack rows into label–value cards (LAY-13).

Badges and tags: labels of ≤ 2 words, pill radius, ≤ 3 per item. Status badges carry text, not just color (A11Y-07). Interactive chips are buttons of ≥ 24 px (touch: LAY-08), and removable chips have a "Remove [label]" button.
Avatars use the sizes 24, 32, 42 and 68 px with an initials fallback. `alt` is the person's name, or empty when the name is shown next to it (A11Y-06).

Choice controls are native inputs (restyled with `appearance: none`, or visually hidden with a styled label). The visible box is ≥ 20 px, and the label is part of a touch-target hit area (LAY-08). Radios serve 2–6 visible options; more options use a select. Groups use `fieldset` and `legend`. Toggle switches only for settings that take effect immediately (`role="switch"`), with a label naming the setting.
verify: Keyboard and screen reader test; touch test

rule: Native `<select>` by default; custom comboboxes follow the APG combobox pattern. Known dates (e.g. birthday) are typed with the format shown; scheduling uses a picker that also accepts typing. File upload uses a native input, with drag and drop as an optional extra (A11Y-14). Accepted types and size limits are stated before upload, with progress and a remove option per file. `type`, `inputmode`, `autocomplete` and `enterkeyhint` bring up the right mobile keyboard (A11Y-16).
verify: Device test on iOS and Android; keyboard test

rule: Form layout: one column on every tier. Two short, related fields may sit side by side from 600 px (postcode and city). Field width hints at the expected input length, labels sit above (DES-20) with help text below, and the required-field marker is explained. The submit button aligns with the field column and is full width on mobile. Never disable the submit button to signal errors; validate on blur and on submit. Long forms show an error summary that links to each field, plus inline errors (A11Y-17).
verify: Form review per tier; failed-submit test

rule: Search: a `<search>` element or `role="search"`, `type="search"`, a visible label or a labelled icon button, and touch-target height (LAY-08). Suggestions follow the APG combobox pattern; Esc closes the suggestions; pressing it again may clear the field. Results pages show the query and the result count. Position: top-right on desktop (PSY-06), in the header or menu panel on mobile.

After a failed submit, focus moves to the error summary or the first invalid field; summary entries link to their fields, and invalid fields carry `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` pointing to the message (A11Y-17).
verify: Keyboard and screen reader failed-submit test

rule: No field blocks paste (no `paste` handler calling `preventDefault()`), and no script filters keystrokes. `maxlength` below the real limit only with a visible character count. Whitespace is trimmed and spaces or dashes in phone numbers and postcodes are normalized, not rejected ([house]).
verify: Grep paste handlers; paste `" 10 115 "` and `"+49 30-123"` into each field type

rule: Sign-in uses `autocomplete="username"` and `current-password`, sign-up and reset `new-password`. One-time codes use one field (`inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code"`), never split digit boxes, and accept paste. Emails, usernames, codes and URLs set `spellcheck="false"` and `autocapitalize="none"`.
verify: Password manager fill; paste a 6-digit code; iOS code suggestion

rule: [house] Inputs, selects and textareas render at ≥ 16 px font size on touch devices, so iOS does not zoom on focus; zoom is never disabled to avoid it (A11Y-08).
verify: Computed font size at 390 px; focus each field on an iPhone

rule: Every form is a `<form>` with a real `type="submit"` button, so Enter submits from single-line fields; in a textarea Enter adds a line, and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter submits where quick entry matters, with a visible hint.

*(orders, payments, sign-ups)* Submit stays enabled and focusable; after the first activation it is `aria-disabled` with a loading state (CMP-21) and ignores repeats. The server de-duplicates retries (idempotency key or one-time form token, ⚗ IETF draft). Input survives an error.
verify: Double-click and Enter twice on throttled 4G: exactly one record

rule: `autofocus` only where one input is the page's task (search, sign-in), on desktop only, never skipping the page heading; dialogs follow CMP-11.

Dialogs, drawers, sheets and inner scroll areas set `overscroll-behavior: contain` so scrolling never chains to the page; never `overscroll-behavior: none` page-wide ([house], it disables swipe navigation).
verify: Scroll to the end of a panel on touch and trackpad: the page stays still

rule: Password fields offer a show/hide toggle (a button with `aria-pressed`); paste and password managers stay allowed (CMP-28, A11Y-20).

Essential content (price, availability, date, name, error text) is never clamped or cut with an ellipsis; any other truncated text is reachable by keyboard and touch, not only via a `title` tooltip; chip and tag rows wrap before they shrink.
verify: 200 % zoom and 320 px with long-string fixtures

rule: Dialogs use `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or the APG modal dialog pattern. Focus moves into the dialog and stays there, Esc closes it, and focus returns to the trigger. The dialog is labelled by its title and has a visible close button (touch target, LAY-08); the background is inert and does not scroll. Widths: 400, 560 or 800 px on desktop; full screen below 600 px with safe-area padding (LAY-09). Dialogs never open on page load, except mandatory gates (UX-17). Destructive confirmations name the action ("Delete project", not "OK").
verify: Keyboard and screen reader test per tier

rule: Drawers are ≤ 400 px wide: navigation slides in from the start, filters and cart from the end. On mobile, bottom sheets have a drag handle plus a close button (A11Y-14). Modal drawers follow CMP-11.

Toasts only confirm non-critical events (`role="status"`). Blocking errors appear inline or in an alert (`role="alert"`, A11Y-17). [house] Toasts stay ≥ 5 s, pause on hover and focus, and persist until dismissed if they contain an action; any auto-dismiss can be turned off or extended (WCAG 2.2.1). Status messages are announced (WCAG 4.1.3). At most 3 stack at once: bottom-center on mobile (above bottom bars and safe areas), bottom-end on desktop, never covering the primary action or the focused element. Inline alerts span their container with an icon, text and an optional action; non-critical alerts can be dismissed.

Tooltips hold short supplemental text only: no interactive content and nothing essential. They show on both hover and focus, can be dismissed with Esc, can be hovered and stay open while hovered (WCAG 1.4.13). On touch devices use a toggletip button or inline text instead. Popovers with interactive content use the `popover` attribute or an APG disclosure or dialog pattern, stay inside the viewport and flip at its edges.

Tabs follow the APG tabs pattern (arrow keys move between tabs, Tab moves into the panel, `aria-selected`), with ≤ 6 tabs. Tabs switch views within one page; navigation between pages uses links. On mobile, tabs scroll horizontally with a visible overflow cue or become an accordion.
verify: Keyboard and screen reader test; 360 px test

rule: Accordions use `<details>`/`<summary>` or the APG accordion pattern (a button inside a heading, `aria-expanded`). The whole header row is clickable at touch-target height (LAY-08), the chevron reflects the state, and several panels may be open at once. Collapsed content stays findable with find-in-page (`<details>` or `hidden="until-found"`). Price, legal and safety information is never collapsed on desktop.

Avoid carousels for key content. If used: visible previous/next buttons and slide indicators (touch targets, LAY-08), "Slide x of y" labels, no autoplay, or autoplay with a pause button that also stops on hover and focus (WCAG 2.2.2). Swiping is never the only control (WCAG 2.5.1). Use CSS scroll snap, with the next slide peeking on mobile.
verify: Keyboard, screen reader and touch test

rule: Lists of more than 24 items paginate with real links (`<a href="?page=2">`, SEO-14), "Page x of y" and previous/next controls at touch-target size (LAY-08); mobile shows previous, current and next. "Load more" and infinite scroll keep paginated URLs, move focus to the first new item and leave the footer reachable.

Multi-step flows show "Step x of y" with step names (≤ 7 steps; mobile shows only the current step's name) and allow going back without losing data, never asking again for data already given (A11Y-18). Progress bars use `<progress>` or `role="progressbar"` with a value.

Breadcrumbs (UX-03): `nav` labelled "Breadcrumb" containing an `ol`, separators drawn in CSS, and the current page as plain text with `aria-current="page"`. On mobile, show only the parent link ("← Parent") or let the trail scroll horizontally.

State components (UX-10): skeletons match the final layout's dimensions (no layout shift, PRF-01), appear only when loading takes > 300 ms and, once shown, stay at least 300 ms ([house], no flicker), and drop the shimmer under reduced motion (A11Y-10). A loading button keeps its width and sets `aria-busy`. Empty states say why there is no content and offer one action. Error states say what happened and how to fix it, and offer a retry. Changes are announced through a live region (A11Y-17).

Video and audio players: native controls or a keyboard-operable player with captions (A11Y-09), a poster image (PRF-09), reserved aspect ratio (PRF-07), full container width, and no autoplay with sound.
Maps load behind a click-to-load placeholder (TEC-21), never trap keyboard or scroll focus, and come with the address as text plus a directions link.

Pricing tables: ≤ 4 plans (PSY-04), one recommended plan marked with a text label (not just color), feature rows in the same order in every plan, and price with billing period and tax status (PSY-13). On mobile, plans stack with the recommended one first, or sit in a scroll-snap row; the full comparison follows CMP-04.
Testimonials (PSY-12): quotes of ≤ 50 words with name, role and photo. Logo walls use one treatment (monochrome or original colors) and are sized by optical area; at most 2 rows on mobile.

Consent banner layout (PRV-02): accept and reject share one button tier and size, both reachable by keyboard before any other control. The banner never hides the focused element (A11Y-12). It sits at the bottom of the screen on mobile within the LAY-20 budget; a full-screen sheet only if it carries no non-essential tracking before choice (PRV-01). The footer link reopens it (LAY-19).
